title: 5 big analyst AI moves: Muse AI seen as major catalyst for Meta; MSFT upgraded - Yahoo! Finance Canada
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results Investing.com -- Here are the biggest analyst moves in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for this week. Stifel this week upgraded Microsoft stock to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $575 from $530, voicing increasing confidence that the company can sustain mid-to-upper-teens revenue growth. Analysts led by Brad Reback said Microsoft "clearly turned the corner post the June quarter print," pointing to sustained Azure upside, reduced large-language-model research intensity and accelerating contribution from OpenAI. Stifel expects 200 to 300 basis points of further Azure upside as Microsoft achieves "a more sustained efficiency cadence across the stack from silicon, models and software," aided by CFO Amy Hood's disclosure that Microsoft has cut "dock-to-live times" by more than 50% over the past year, helping capacity convert to revenue faster. Copilot seat count reached roughly 30 million in the fourth quarter, up 10 million quarter-over-quarter, while GitHub's shift to consumption-based pricing adds another growth lever. These tailwinds should offset moderating seat growth as Microsoft 365 approaches 500 million seats, sustaining at least mid-teens growth for several years, the analysts said. Earlier concerns about margin compression proved "too negative," the analysts said, pointing to Azure efficiency gains, the elimination of revenue-share payments to OpenAI after an April contract revision, and an extension of asset useful life to 25 years from 15. Microsoft's need to aggressively invest in its own large-language-model development is also "abating" as open-weight models deliver comparable outcomes at lower cost. Citi remains overweight equities led by the U.S., saying it would add more stock market exposure if shares pull back, even as higher oil prices, rising rates and poor seasonals weigh on sentiment. "We are impressed how well the equity market has been trading in the light of higher oil, higher rates, and poor seasonals in Sep, even at a time when volatility in U.S. rates is rising," the bank's strategists wrote in their September house views. They noted stocks usually pull back after the Fed's first rate hike rather than before it, and that markets also tend to weaken ahead of midterm elections before the usual year-end rally. "We prefer the U.S. as we still believe that the AI trade will continue," the strategists wrote, adding that the U.S. is also better protected from further rises in oil prices. Emerging Asia, cut in early July, is Citi's next choice when it adds risk. In bonds, Citi remains neutral on duration, long emerging markets and short European government bonds. The upcoming French election adds to European risks, and the bank moved U.K. gilts back to neutral. "At this stage, it is unclear to us what it will take to stop a hawkish Fed," the strategists said. Citi stayed underweight investment-grade credit in the U.S. and Europe as a hedge for its equity overweight. In commodities, it remains long base metals and neutral on energy, having recently cut its gold long, and moved emerging market currencies back to neutral given rising U.S. rate volatility. Wall Street analysts were broadly positive on Meta following its Connect event, where the company made its Muse AI agent the centerpiece of its product and hardware plans. Evercore ISI kept its Outperform rating and $860 price target, calling Meta its top long idea. "Muse over Metaverse is a good thing for META investors," the analysts wrote, adding that Muse could lead investors to value the stock at 25 to 30 times 2028 earnings, taking shares to $1,000 or more. The broker compared the moment to Alphabet's own AI transition: "Just like GOOGL in 2025, what we are witnessing is a transition from a perceived 'AI Loser' to an 'AI Winner.'" Raymond James analyst Josh Beck raised his price target to $860, based on 20 times 2028 earnings, citing Muse downloads of more than 300,000 a day and a base case of more than $50 billion in revenue against annual costs of about $12 billion. Separately, Mizuho's Lloyd Walmsley, who has an Outperform rating and $750 target, said Muse Charm — a keychain-like device expected before the holidays — could accelerate user growth further. "Meta's AI product has significant momentum," he wrote, though he was more cautious on Meta's new $1,299 VR glasses due to their high price. Citi also kept its Buy rating and $800 target, saying it is more positive on the shares after the event, while JPMorgan said Muse could become the most widely used consumer AI app since ChatGPT. In a separate note, Citi has raised its price target on Micron to $1,300 from $1,150, expecting the stock to rally into the SEMICON West conference and anticipating upside to results and guidance when the company reports. The bank lifted its August and November-quarter estimates on better-than-expected blended DRAM pricing, now modeling fiscal fourth-quarter sales and EPS of $51 billion and $31.45, above consensus. Micron's stock "has made a large round trip since last earnings, falling 35% from the prior high and rebounding 34% from the July low," Citi analysts said, pointing to SEMICON West as the next catalyst. At the conference, Citi anticipates equipment makers will flag shortages of DRAM, MLCC, printed circuit boards and optical components, a potential bottleneck in the tools used to manufacture memory chips. Those constraints could limit DRAM and NAND supply growth to the low-20% range and help push memory prices higher into next year, with both markets expected to remain undersupplied on strong AI-driven demand and prices likely peaking in Q2 2027. Citi assumes blended DRAM average selling prices rise 20% and 13% quarter-on-quarter in the current and following periods, with NAND up 34% and 15%, and expects enterprise SSD demand driven by AI inference to offset softer consumer NAND. Also this week, Rosenblatt initiated coverage of SanDisk with a Buy rating and a $2,400 price target, arguing that AI is transforming NAND flash memory from a commodity into a critical piece of computing infrastructure. Analyst Kevin Cassidy said new AI compute platforms are creating an opportunity to reposition NAND "from a commodity storage medium to a more system-critical component of AI infrastructure," as expanding model sizes and data-intensive inference prioritize density, performance, endurance and supply certainty over the lowest price. Cassidy pointed to SanDisk's BiCS8 and BiCS10 platforms, developed with manufacturing partner Kioxia over some 25 years, as supporting that shift — improving density with fewer 3D layers than some rivals, sustaining a cost and performance advantage in AI-oriented enterprise storage. New business model agreements with eight of the largest NAND customers, potentially covering about 65% of fiscal 2028 production, should improve demand visibility and reduce historical sector volatility, he added. Management's fiscal 2028-to-2030 framework calls for mid-to-high-teens revenue growth, roughly 80% non-GAAP gross margin and a 50% adjusted free-cash-flow margin. Cassidy conservatively estimated fiscal 2030 non-GAAP earnings of about $300 a share. His $2,400 target is based on 10 times his fiscal 2028 earnings estimate, a multiple he called conservative given the growth outlook, while reflecting execution risk and the chance NAND reverts to cyclical, commodity-like pricing. 5 big analyst AI moves: Muse AI seen as major catalyst for Meta; MSFT upgraded China consumer stocks near decade lows as investors pile into AI Boeing finds 737 MAX software glitch that may affect automated navigation - WSJ Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results

title: pladis engaged users save 12+ hours a month on average with Microsoft 365 Copilot - Microsoft
content: Across pladis, colleagues spent hours each week on routine tasks such as drafting content, summarizing documents, and building reports. The business needed a structured, measurable way to help teams work more efficiently and build confidence in AI. Through its "Steal Back 10 Hours" program, pladis gave colleagues Microsoft 365 Copilot inside Outlook, Teams, Word, and Excel, added Power Platform agents, and drove adoption alongside partner Mindworks, delivering training and masterclasses. Out of 70 colleagues trained, the 48 who completed all masterclasses and the company’s productivity tracker reported saving 580 hours a month, averaging just over 12 hours each against a 10-hour target, with some reporting up to 20 hours saved. “There was a fear around AI. Now we’ve turned it into a completely positive environment.” Merve Gülşen, Head of Digital Technology, pladis Global Headquartered in London, pladis is a global snacking brand with more than 180 years of baking heritage. Home to brands including McVitie's, GODIVA, and Ülker, it employs around 16,000 people and reaches consumers in more than 110 markets, guided by a simple purpose to bring happiness with every bite. But delivering on that promise at global scale meant finding smarter ways to support teams, reducing time spent on routine tasks so people could focus more of their energy on creativity, collaboration, and decision-making. Across HR, finance, procurement, marketing, R&D, and operations, colleagues spent hours each week drafting content, summarizing documents, building reports, and handling routine requests. There was a clear opportunity for pladis to help teams work more efficiently, but experience and confidence in AI varied across the business. Without a coordinated approach, adoption risked becoming fragmented and inconsistent, and some colleagues remained understandably cautious about the technology. In 2025, pladis set out to deliver a structured and measurable way to reshape everyday work, building the skills and confidence to do it, and proving the payoff to leadership. At the heart of its approach was Microsoft 365 Copilot, which brought AI directly into the tools employees already used every day, such as Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Rather than positioning AI as an experimental add-on, pladis made it a practical productivity accelerator inside existing workflows. People could draft content faster, summarize meetings and long documents in seconds, analyze data more efficiently and strip out repetitive administration. All without learning a new system. Its "Steal Back 10 Hours" initiative helped accelerate this further, with an eight-week program that paired hands-on training with careful measurement of the productivity gains each participant achieved. Its goal? To reclaim the time lost to mundane tasks and reinvest it in the thinking that only people can do. "We use AI to help eliminate repetitive work and give our people more time to focus on strategic and critical thinking at pladis," says Nataliya Otluoglu, VP of Data, AI, and Digital Transformation. "Copilot enhances how our employees work today." Nataliya Otluoglu, VP of Data, AI, and Digital Transformation, pladis Global To make adoption stick, pladis surrounded the technology with people. It created an internal AI community, appointed AI champions and advocates across departments, ran office hours and masterclasses, and established governance to support the whole effort. Partner Mindworks delivered training and enablement sessions, answered questions, and supported colleagues as they turned ideas into working use cases. "We had to find a great partner," recalls Merve Gülşen, Head of Digital Technology. "We connected with Microsoft, and they brought us Mindworks. We structured everything and put the right governance around it." This kept momentum high and prevented sessions from being derailed by highly technical questions. From there, pladis moved beyond individual productivity toward process-level impact. It drew on Microsoft Power Platform, including Copilot Studio, Power Automate, and Power BI to digitize recurring workflows and create purpose-built agents. For example, at the pladis site in Carlisle, home to one of the world’s oldest biscuit factories, the health, safety, and environment team built an AI risk-assessing agent using Copilot Studio. "It allowed us to take photos of a task being done or an area, and the AI agent would review that information, compare it to UK health and safety guidance, and give us a formatted response," explains Paul McConnell, Health, Safety and Environment Manager. In procurement, teams turned to agents to stay on top of fast-changing market conditions and map supply risk. "AI agents are incredible," says Usman Zafar, Global Procurement Manager. "They help me a lot with managing market insight in real time, with all publicly available data in one place." Usman Zafar, Global Procurement Manager, pladis Global The impact was fast and measurable. The first cohort set out to reclaim 10 hours per person per month. Of the 70 people trained, 48 completed all masterclasses and the productivity gain tracker. Together, they reported saving 580 hours a month, averaging just over 12 hours each, with some colleagues reporting savings as high as 20 hours a month.  At Carlisle, the safety agent alone saved an estimated 800 hours each year. Just as important as the numbers was the shift in mindset. What began with hesitation became genuine enthusiasm, with employees identifying new use cases and advocating for AI across their departments. Proof that the culture had changed, not just the tooling. “There was a fear around AI,” admits Gülşen. “Now we’ve turned it into a completely positive environment.” 12+ hrs saved per engaged colleague a month on average With the model proven, pladis is scaling enterprise-wide, expanding Copilot and Power Platform to new cohorts, regions and functions, and evolving its licensing to unlock more advanced AI and security capabilities. "Rather than focusing on one individual task, we want to look into the end-to-end process as a whole," explains Zafar. As it looks to the future, pladis is keeping its heritage firmly in view. "We need to protect our brands so they continue to be trusted and protect our relationship with our customers," says Otluoglu. "Our focus is to increase AI literacy across the organization and modernize how we work today without losing what makes us distinctive and agile." “It allowed us to take photos of a task being done or an area, and the AI agent would review that information.” Paul McConnell, Health, Safety and Environment Manager, pladis Global Our mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. title: QCOM Stock Eyes Worst Month In 7 Years: Analyst Says MSFT, GOOG May Be Behind Qualcomm’s AI Momentum - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Qualcomm, Inc. (QCOM) are poised to post their worst monthly run in years, but an analyst’s bull case suggests that the company’s AI data-center ambitions may already be gaining support from major cloud customers. QCOM stock has declined 18% so far this month, on track for its weakest week since April 2019. Shares are also on track to end the week in the red, with the stock down 2% in overnight trading heading into Friday. Morningstar raised its fair value estimate for Qualcomm to $200 from $155 after the company hosted an investor event focused on its emerging data center chip business. The firm said Qualcomm’s data center revenue forecast was “better than we expected.” Qualcomm now expects $5 billion in data center revenue in fiscal 2027 and $15 billion in fiscal 2029. “Two hyperscale customers will exceed $1 billion in fiscal 2027, which intrigues us,” Morningstar said. The firm added that Qualcomm’s server CPU deal with Meta is “presumably not included,” since that business is expected to ramp up in the second half of 2028. “Microsoft and Google presented at the event, and perhaps these are the two immediate customers,” Morningstar said. Morningstar said Qualcomm’s forecast and signed deals suggest its AI initiatives will gain adoption with leading customers “ahead of our expectations.” Earlier this week, Qualcomm raised its fiscal 2029 non-handset revenue target to $40 billion as part of its broader diversification push. The company also targeted $10 billion in automotive revenue, more than $14 billion in IoT revenue and more than $15 billion in data center revenue by fiscal 2029. Qualcomm said handsets are expected to represent one-third of QCT revenue by then. The AI optimism comes as Qualcomm faces a major smartphone headwind from Apple’s in-house modem push. Morningstar called Apple’s move to displace Qualcomm a “looming headwind, but not a death blow,” citing the company’s expansion into automotive, PC, IoT and data center processors. Qualcomm expects its modem share within Apple’s iPhone 18 series to fall to just 20% in fiscal 2027. Morningstar estimates that would cut Qualcomm’s Apple chip revenue to about $2 billion, from more than $6 billion just two years earlier. Still, Morningstar expects data-center AI revenue to help offset the decline in Apple. Morningstar also cautioned that Qualcomm is not about to dethrone Nvidia: “We don’t anticipate it will usurp Nvidia’s wide moat or early-mover advantage in AI.” Morningstar said even a modest share of the massive AI computing market could support Qualcomm’s earnings growth.
